newsitem.title: CHINA: Shell China refinery venture seen revived in April.
newsitem.headline: Shell China refinery venture seen revived in April.

text.p: A revised proposal to build a petrochemical plant and refinery with the Royal Dutch/Shell Group will be submitted to China's planners this month, a senior China National Offshore Corp (CNOOC) official said on Monday.

"We will be submitting an amended feasibility study to build the petrochemical plant first and the refinery later," Wu Mengfei, a director in the Planning and Treasury Department, told Reuters. He said it would be submitted in April.
The refinery part of a US$6 billion complex in southern Guandong province, first proposed in the late 1980s, was initially dropped in February.
Wu would not provide further details of the revised proposal but said his state-owned company expected a favourable response from China's State Planning Commission.

Shell would still hold a 50 percent stake and CNOOC 20 percent. China's Guangdong provincial government, China Merchant Holdings Co and state refiner Sinopec would each hold a 10-percent interest, Wu said.
China said in January it would look at foreign proposals for refinery projects on a case-by-case basis. It also said it would not rule out new refineries, despite concerns about over-capacity.
But China also told executives of Mobil Corp it was not encouraging new joint venture refineries and would rather expand domestic refineries.
China's only joint venture refinery with foreign interest is the Dalian West Pacific Petrochemical Corp where Total of France holds a 20-percent stake.
